title: C.R.E.A.M. and the Charmels
hook: C.R.E.A.M. is really a 1967 Charmels record.
voiceover: C.R.E.A.M. is really a 1967 Charmels record. The Charmels were a Stax group out of Memphis. In 1967 they cut a single on Volt called As Long As I've Got You, written by Isaac Hayes and David Porter. It wasn't a hit. 26 years later RZA pulled the piano from the intro, looped it, and laid it under Raekwon and Inspectah Deck. That's the whole record. No chorus melody, just that piano rolling over the drums. What changed is the context. A forgotten Memphis soul intro became the sound of Staten Island in 1993. Save this, then go pull the original and hear what RZA left out. What flip should I break down Thursday?
caption: Day 1. The record behind the record, every day, from behind the decks. C.R.E.A.M. (Wu-Tang Clan, Loud, 1993) sits on the piano intro of As Long As I've Got You by The Charmels (Volt, 1967), written by Isaac Hayes and David Porter. RZA kept the piano, changed the world around it. Save this before you go pull the original. Which flip do you want Thursday? 🎹
